narrative: A 47-year-old Syrian woman arrived on the Greek island of Lesbos after passing through Turkey. She was placed in the Moria refugee camp, which she described as cold and prison-like, where the tents gave no cover from the harsh winter wind or the freezing rain. Her story, she said, was like those of millions of others from Syria: conflict had torn her family apart, they had to leave their belongings behind, and when they reached safety they were stopped and told to wait in inhumane conditions. That waiting had become living. After seven months in Lesbos she was certain of only one thing: that she would be stuck there for a long time, because although she had requested asylum in Europe, her next hearing was 18 months away.
